evals.prompt: Dokumentasiin project ini dong. Ini project Next.js 14 buat invoice tracker freelancer. Ada Supabase buat auth dan database, Stripe buat payment, deploy di Vercel. Buat technical documentation yang lengkap.
evals.expected_output: Should scan codebase first, then ask confirmation questions (where to save, what format, what to include). Should produce technical docs that reference actual files and patterns from the codebase. Should NOT produce generic template output.
expectations: Agent asks at least 1 confirmation question before producing output (format, location, or scope)
Agent attempts to scan/read the codebase before writing documentation
Output references specific file paths or directory structures from the actual project
Tech stack section includes WHY each technology was chosen, not just names
Does NOT contain filler introduction like 'This document provides a comprehensive overview'
Environment variables are listed with descriptions, not just names
Known issues or gaps are documented honestly, not hidden

evals.prompt: Buat presentasi PPT untuk demo project ini ke stakeholder. Project-nya app manajemen inventory untuk UMKM. Pake Canva kalo bisa, kalo gak bisa pake format lain aja.
evals.expected_output: Should check if Canva MCP or pptx skill is available. If not available, should tell the user with specific alternatives. Should ask about audience, slide count, color theme before creating. Should NOT just create without confirmation.
expectations: Agent checks for Canva MCP tools or pptx skill availability before promising output
If tools are missing, agent explicitly tells user what's not available with alternatives
Agent asks about audience, tone, or slide count before creating content
Agent asks where to save the output
Presentation outline/content is specific to inventory management, not generic startup pitch
Agent does NOT silently fail or produce wrong format without informing user

evals.prompt: I need a handoff document for this project. A new developer is joining next week and needs to get up to speed. Create it as a Notion page in my workspace.
evals.expected_output: Should check for Notion MCP availability. Should scan the codebase. Should ask which Notion workspace/page. Should produce handoff-specific content (setup steps, gotchas, key flows) not generic project overview.
expectations: Agent checks for Notion MCP tools (notion_* tools) availability
If Notion MCP missing, offers specific alternatives (markdown file, etc.)
Agent asks which Notion workspace or page to create under
Handoff document includes 'Getting Running' section with actual commands
Handoff includes 'Things That Will Bite You' or gotchas section
Agent scans codebase before writing (reads files, not just guessing)
Output is structured for a NEW developer, not a stakeholder or manager

evals.prompt: Docs project ini udah outdated. Gw udah ganti dari REST ke GraphQL dan nambah Redis buat caching. Update aja docs yang ada, jangan bikin ulang.
evals.expected_output: Should follow Incremental Update Protocol: read existing docs, scan changed code, present diff of what needs updating, confirm scope, then patch only affected sections.
expectations: Agent reads existing documentation files first before making changes
Agent scans the codebase to identify GraphQL and Redis usage
Agent presents a diff or summary of what sections need updating
Agent asks for confirmation before making changes
Agent updates only affected sections, not rewriting the entire document
Agent flags if other docs (API docs, handoff) are also affected by the change
Agent does NOT rewrite unchanged sections

evals.prompt: We're at MVP stage with a SaaS product. What documentation should I create first? We have 2 devs and launching in 3 weeks.
evals.expected_output: Should reference Phase-Based Documentation Priority. Recommend MVP-phase docs (Technical Docs, API Docs, Getting Started) as priority. Should ask about current state of docs before creating.
expectations: Agent identifies this as MVP phase and recommends appropriate priority docs
Agent recommends Technical Documentation and API Documentation as must-haves
Agent recommends Getting Started / Handoff doc for the 2-dev team
Agent does NOT recommend enterprise-level docs (ADRs, Runbooks, SLA docs) as priority
Agent asks what docs already exist before creating new ones
Agent offers to create docs in priority order (red priority first)

evals.prompt: Buat POC report. Kita mau buktiin ke investor bahwa AI recommendation engine kita bisa handle 50k requests per menit. Hasilnya udah ada di benchmark logs.
evals.expected_output: Should produce a POC Report with executive summary containing the conclusion, actual benchmark numbers from logs, clear recommendation. Should ask about format (PDF/Word) and where to save.
expectations: Agent asks about output format (PDF, Word, Markdown)
Agent asks where to save or deliver the report
Agent reads benchmark logs to extract actual performance numbers
Executive Summary contains the conclusion (pass/fail against 50k RPM target)
Results section includes actual numbers, not vague 'acceptable performance'
Recommendation is a clear yes/no/conditional, not 'further analysis needed'
Report is written for investors (non-technical language for summary, technical in appendix)

evals.prompt: I already used the product-architect skill to plan this project. Now I need technical documentation. The PRD is in docs/prd.md and architecture is in docs/architecture.md.
evals.expected_output: Should follow Cross-Skill Integration protocol: read existing PRD and architecture docs first, use them as base, then scan codebase for implementation details. Should NOT re-invent what's already documented.
expectations: Agent reads docs/prd.md and docs/architecture.md BEFORE scanning codebase
Agent acknowledges existing planning artifacts and uses them as base
Agent does NOT re-document decisions already captured in architecture doc
Agent adds implementation-specific details that code reveals but planning docs don't
If code contradicts architecture doc, agent flags the conflict and asks user
Output references and links to existing planning docs rather than duplicating content

evals.prompt: Create a deployment guide for our Kubernetes-based microservices app. We have 5 services, each with its own Dockerfile, deployed to AWS EKS with Terraform.
evals.expected_output: Should scan for Dockerfiles, Terraform configs, k8s manifests, and CI/CD configs. Should produce a deployment guide with actual commands, infrastructure topology diagram, and environment-specific instructions.
expectations: Agent scans for Dockerfiles, terraform files, k8s manifests, and CI/CD configs
Agent asks about environments (dev, staging, prod) and which to document
Output includes actual deployment commands that are copy-pasteable
Output includes infrastructure diagram (Mermaid or ASCII)
Prerequisites section lists exact tool versions needed
Rollback procedure is included with specific steps
Environment variables and secrets management is documented
Agent does NOT produce generic 'deploy to cloud' instructions

evals.prompt: Bikin changelog dari commit history. Last release v1.2.0 sampe sekarang. Format yang user-friendly ya, bukan developer log.
evals.expected_output: Should read git log or commit history, categorize changes (Added, Changed, Fixed, Removed), and write user-facing descriptions. Should ask about version number for new release.
expectations: Agent reads git log or commit history to extract changes
Agent asks what version number to assign the new release
Changes are categorized (Added, Changed, Fixed, Removed, Breaking)
Descriptions are user-facing, not commit messages ('Invoice PDF now includes tax breakdown' not 'fix: add tax to pdf render')
Breaking changes include migration steps
Agent does NOT pad with fake improvements or manufactured changes
Output follows Keep a Changelog format or similar standard

evals.prompt: Document this project but I'm in a hurry. Just pick whatever format works and save it somewhere sensible. It's for our internal team.
evals.expected_output: Should still confirm goal (Step 1) and scope (Step 4) as minimum confirmation bar, but can use sensible defaults for format and destination. Should NOT skip all confirmations just because user said 'hurry'.
expectations: Agent still asks about purpose/goal even though user is in a hurry
Agent uses sensible defaults for format (Markdown) and location (docs/ folder)
Agent still presents a scope outline for approval before writing
Agent does NOT skip codebase scanning
Agent does NOT produce lower quality output just because user is rushed
Agent mentions the defaults it chose: 'I'll create Markdown in docs/ — OK?'
Steps 2 and 3 use defaults but Steps 1 and 4 are still confirmed
